result.title: Memphis: A Case Study in Seeding an Agent Task from a Model's Real-World Attempt
result.comment: 23 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables. Task, code, trials and data: https://github.com/ia03/memphis-task
result.summary: Agent benchmarks are usually made harder by scaling up the data their tasks are built from, yet models that do well on them still fail at real work. We propose building simulated tasks from a model's own attempt at an open-ended task in the real world, so that the model's failures in the simulation resemble its failures in reality. As a case study, we had GPT-6.1 Sol manage two human workers in Cairo over chat for five shifts, with a budget of 7,000 Egyptian pounds, to build as many USB desk lamps as it could. It built two. From the real-world attempt's transcript, we build Memphis, an evaluation in a model-simulated world. Memphis is hard: GPT-6.1 Sol delivers 1.0 lamp per trial on average and repeats its real-world mistakes, buying too few stands and giving up the search for them. With a one-page hint on where to buy parts and who can wire them, it delivers 9.2. Claude Opus 5.5 delivers 2.2 without the hint and 4.6 with it. We release the task, the trials, the audits, and a redacted record of the real-world evaluation.

AI.brief_summary: 该文以 GPT-6.1 Sol 管理工人、在预算内制作 USB 台灯的真实尝试为种子，构建模型模拟环境基准 Memphis，并比较有无采购提示时各模型的表现与失败复现情况。
AI.relevance_reason: 「用模型自身真实失败轨迹生成仿真任务以复现失败模式」的做法，可能为 LVR 的证据搜索、过早停止与评测任务构造提供间接启发；但论文不涉及视觉或 latent 推理机制，联系较远，需核查。
